problem: Removing the backwards-time guard from _observe lets a decreasing `now` reach _in_window, whose left-only eviction assumes sorted deques, so stale entries stay counted (false denials, wrong remaining/retry_after) and a stale or huge `now` can bypass or lock out a key.
The change removes an error-contract guarantee with no test pinning the old or new behaviour for a decreasing `now`.
_last_now is write-only and _observe is a no-op wrapper after the guard removal, so both are dead code.
`now` is never validated, so NaN, inf or non-numeric values reach the eviction logic and a NaN entry blocks eviction for that key permanently (pre-existing).
_in_window creates and stores an empty deque per key, including for read-only calls, and never deletes them, so _accepted grows without bound (pre-existing).
